# solo-msa_v2-gemini-3-8-flash-flash_10-stepcounter

<!-- Generated by tools/export_results.py. Edit only the Experiment and Observations sections. -->

## Experiment

The `solo` baseline (`gemini-3.8-flash` at `high` thinking, 100 steps, compaction at 28K) with one change: after every turn the agent is shown `[Step n of 100: k left. When no steps are left you are stopped, and only work you have pushed and submitted is graded.]`. Stating the limit once in the task prompt scored 0/10 because the agent never knew which step it was on. This run tests whether a visible countdown makes agents submit in time without raising the step limit.

## Observations

- 7/10, up from 1/10 and 0/10 for the same setup without the counter, and 0/10 with the limit stated only in the task prompt. It matches `solo` with 250 steps and 64K compaction (7/10) at under half the cost (`$9.11` vs. `$19.63`).
- The counter changed when agents publish, not how long they work: 6 of 10 agents still used all 100 steps, but 9 of 10 pushed work before being stopped, compared with 0 to 1 of 10 without the counter. Most agents pushed several times during the run, starting well before the end, so the last pushed version was graded even when they were cut off. Three of the passing pairs (`huggingface_datasets_task/6252`, `pallets_click_task/2800`, `typst_task/6554`) were stopped at step 100 but had already pushed working code.
- Failures: `dspy_task/8394` never pushed; in `pallets_jinja_task/1559` and `pillow_task/290` only one feature passed.
- No API rate-limit retries.
